title: Kushner Albania Resort Built on Land from Drug Trafficker with Forged Deeds — "Flamingo Revolution" Protests
description_short: Kushner Albania Resort Built on Land from Drug Trafficker with Forged Deeds — "Flamingo Revolution" Protests
description_medium: Albanian anti-corruption prosecutors are investigating whether deeds for protected coastal land planned for a Jared Kushner-backed resort were forged. The seller, Artur Shehu, faces separate allegations of drug trafficking and money laundering, which he denies. Reuters found no evidence that Kushner or other project backers knew of suspicions when the land was sold. The allegations remain under investigation.
description_long: Albania’s anti-corruption prosecution service is examining whether title deeds for protected coastal land intended for a resort backed by Jared Kushner’s business were forged. The land was sold to Albania Land Development in April by Miami-based Artur Shehu. Prosecutors separately allege that Shehu and associates used proceeds from cocaine trafficking and falsified titles; his lawyer denies the allegations and says the family lawfully owned the land. Reuters, whose reporting Al Jazeera republished, said roughly 110 million euros tied to the sale had been frozen in a notary’s account and found no evidence that Kushner or other project backers knew of suspicions when the land changed hands. CBS reported that SPAK’s investigation of Shehu includes allegations of drug trafficking and money laundering and said the inquiry did not concern a Kushner-associated company. Residents continue to challenge Shehu’s ownership in court. The resort proposal has drawn protests over development near protected wetlands and coast. The criminal allegations remain under investigation, not established findings.
organization_tags: Special Structure Against Corruption and Organized Crime (SPAK)

title: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
description_short: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
description_medium: Reuters reported on August 13, 2025, that Chinese buyers had booked about 8 million metric tons of South American soybeans for September and 4 million tons for October, half of expected demand. U.S. exporters risked missing their usual fall sales window amid unresolved trade talks and a 23% Chinese tariff. Brazil was filling the near-term supply period.
description_long: China's retaliatory tariffs in 2025 reduced U.S. agricultural exports to China from $24.5 billion in 2024 to just $8.4 billion in 2025, a two-thirds decline and the lowest annual figure in over two decades, per NDSU Agricultural Trade Monitor analysis. NDSU estimated the annualized China-specific agricultural export shortfall at $14.9 billion — 41% larger than the $10.6 billion shortfall during the 2018–2019 trade war. Soybeans accounted for $6.8 billion of the loss; beef and cotton each contributed $1.3 billion; corn $333 million; and tree nuts $964 million. For the first time in more than 20 years, Chinese importers purchased no soybeans from the U.S. autumn 2025 harvest, forcing American farmers to store their crops as prices fell to a five-year low. Brazil's soybean exports to China hit record levels in 2025, topping 85 million metric tons — an 18% increase — as U.S. market share evaporated.

title: Trump Pardons 1,500+ Jan. 6 Rioters — Including Those Who Attacked Police and Election Workers — on Day One
description_short: Trump Pardons 1,500+ Jan. 6 Rioters — Including Those Who Attacked Police and Election Workers — on Day One
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Trump pardoned all other people convicted of January 6 offenses, commuted named defendants’ sentences to time served, directed prison releases, and ordered the Justice Department to seek dismissal with prejudice of pending indictments. The proclamation treats convicted people and those awaiting trial differently; it does not pardon everyone charged.
description_long: Within hours of his January 20, 2025, inauguration, Trump issued sweeping clemency — full pardons, commutations, or directed dismissals — covering all 1,500-plus people charged in the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack, including hundreds convicted of assaulting police officers, members of the Proud Boys sentenced for seditious conspiracy including Enrique Tarrio who received 22 years, and Oath Keepers leaders convicted of plotting to stop the transfer of power. By the next morning, all 200-plus people in federal custody for January 6 crimes had been released. The DOJ simultaneously dropped all pending January 6 prosecutions, ending the largest criminal prosecution in Justice Department history. Trump separately directed his DOJ to review what it called weaponized prosecutions of his allies, including the case of Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters. The pardons sent a direct signal to future election workers, officials, and vigilantes: attacking democratic processes in the name of Trump carries zero legal risk. Legal experts called it an unprecedented use of the pardon power to erase accountability for an attempt to overturn an election.

title: Trump Retaliates Against Brad Raffensperger and Election Officials Who Refused to Overturn 2020
description_short: Trump Retaliates Against Brad Raffensperger and Election Officials Who Refused to Overturn 2020
description_medium: On March 14, 2025, Trump said people he blamed for the 2020 election “should go to jail.” A later presidential memorandum revoked former CISA director Chris Krebs’s security clearance and directed the Justice Department to review his actions at the agency. The Brennan Center describes these steps as part of pressure on election officials and election administration.
description_long: Throughout 2025 and 2026, Trump and his DOJ constructed an apparatus of retaliation against officials who had certified the 2020 election. In a March 14, 2025 speech, Trump stated: What a difference a rigged and crooked election had on our country. And the people who did this to us should go to jail. An executive order directed DOJ to review the actions of Chris Krebs — Trump's own CISA director — because he denied that the 2020 election was rigged and stolen. The Georgia GOP's June 2025 convention passed a resolution calling for the party to block Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger from qualifying on the Republican ticket for daring to certify Biden's 2020 win. Trump endorsed Raffensperger's opponent Burt Jones — one of the fake electors — for governor. On May 13, 2026, Raffensperger's gubernatorial campaign reported an active threat and a bomb scare at a campaign event; Raffensperger said: When you stand on principle, some people will hate you, even want to try and hurt you. The Brennan Center documented that the administration's threats of prosecution were designed to ensure that election officials facing future pressure would capitulate rather than risk the retaliation Raffensperger endured for doing his job.

title: TRUMP and MELANIA Memecoins: The Presidential Pump-and-Dump That Made $100M in Fees
description_short: TRUMP and MELANIA Memecoins: The Presidential Pump-and-Dump That Made $100M in Fees
description_medium: Reuters reported that Trump launched the $TRUMP token on January 17, 2025, and estimated that its creators had collected $86 million to $100 million in trading fees by January 30. The report said about 200,000 wallets, mostly with small holdings, lost money, while at least 50 large investors made more than $10 million each. Reuters could not determine how much of the fees reached Trump personally.
description_long: On January 17, 2025 — two days before his inauguration — Donald Trump posted on Truth Social announcing the launch of the $TRUMP memecoin, which surged from an opening price of $0.18 to a peak of $75 within 24 hours, generating a market cap exceeding $14.5 billion at its apex. An early trader who purchased 5.97 million tokens within two minutes of the announcement — possibly tipped off in advance, forensic analysts told Wired — walked away with a profit of up to $109 million in two days. Entities behind the coin, including CIC Digital, a Trump affiliate controlling 80% of the token supply, accumulated nearly $100 million in trading fees within two weeks alone, according to analyses by blockchain firms Merkle Science and Chainalysis. The First Lady launched the $MELANIA coin on January 19, with insiders holding 89% of supply in what blockchain analytics firm Bubblemaps identified as a classic pump-and-dump structure. Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci warned: Now, anyone globally can effectively deposit money into the bank account of the President of the United States with just a few clicks. Every favor — be it geopolitical, corporate, or personal — is now openly for sale. By mid-2025, Trump's 2026 financial disclosure revealed CIC Digital had taken in over $600 million from meme coin sales, while retail investors bore catastrophic losses as the coins collapsed more than two-thirds from peak.
